overview: After 1.g3 Nf6 White continues Bg2 and Nf3 (or c4) and usually plays a King's Indian Attack, Réti or English set-up, while Black develops a king's Indian or Queen's Indian style game. Nothing is forced; it is mostly a move order that transposes.

white_ideas.idea: Bg2, Nf3, O-O and d3 or d4 with e4 later
Transpose into a Catalan, Réti or King's Indian Attack

black_ideas.idea: ...d5, ...e6 or ...g6 and a King's Indian style set-up
Seize space with ...d5 and ...e5 and equalise easily

approach.notes: g3 and Bg2 can be played against almost anything.

level.notes: Few moves to learn, plans are clear but not forcing.

character.reason: Quiet but not especially hard to break down.

structure.reason: Flank opening with the centre undecided.

approach.reason: The g3/Bg2 set-up can be played against most replies.

level.reason: Clear plans but vague tension; not obviously beginner.

plans.reason: The Bg2 diagonal is the point.
